status: finite SU(2) character-basis diagonalization with residual and Schur-complement enclosures; convergent one-plaquette gaps but no uniform continuum or volume theorem

convention.fullHamiltonian: H=(2 g^2/a) h_kappa for one open plaquette after maximal-tree gauge fixing
convention.constantWarning: the additive 2 kappa changes absolute energies but not gaps; rescalings in other Hamiltonian conventions must be mapped before comparing numbers

certification.truncation: P_N retains n=0,...,N and Q_N retains n>=N+1
certification.tailFloor: Q_N h Q_N >= T_N Q_N with T_N=((N+1)/2)(((N+1)/2)+1), because kappa(2-chi_1/2) is positive
certification.schurLower: if theta_k<T_N, set delta=kappa^2/(T_N-theta_k); then E_k >= lambda_k(P_N h P_N-delta |N><N|)
certification.residual: extending a normalized Ritz vector by zero gives residual norm rho=kappa |v_N| and dist(theta,spectrum(h))<=rho
certification.gapInterval: E1-E0 lies in [L1-U0,U1-L0] whenever the level enclosures are ordered
certification.certifiedTarget: report convergence when the gap interval has positive lower endpoint and relative width below 1e-8

scanExpectations.strongCouplingLimit: as kappa->0 the gap tends C2(1/2)-C2(0)=3/4
scanExpectations.weakCouplingBasisGrowth: the character distribution broadens and the cutoff needed for a fixed enclosure grows with kappa
scanExpectations.finiteCertification: all listed couplings obtain a positive certified gap interval by some listed cutoff
scanExpectations.residualBehavior: boundary residuals decay rapidly once N exceeds the occupied character range

continuumScalingAudit.weakCouplingQuestion: whether a Delta_H vanishes along a renormalized trajectory so that Delta_H can remain finite as a->0
continuumScalingAudit.onePlaquetteOutcome: the isolated plaquette has only a compact rotor localized by one magnetic well; its lattice-unit gap approaches a nonzero cutoff-scale number rather than generating a four-dimensional infrared scale
continuumScalingAudit.missing: coupled plaquettes, a thermodynamic limit, running coupling, and a uniform lower bound after subtracting extensive vacuum energy

volumeObstruction.basisGrowth: with P independent loop labels and cutoff N, the unreduced tensor-product count grows as (N+1)^P before Gauss-law recoupling
volumeObstruction.boundaryGrowth: many plaquette interactions cross the representation cutoff, so the P-Q coupling norm need not remain kappa
volumeObstruction.tailProblem: the one-coordinate Casimir tail floor does not directly bound the first omitted many-body sector above an extensive interacting vacuum
volumeObstruction.gapProblem: a thermodynamic gap is a difference of two extensive energies and requires errors that cancel or remain uniform in volume
volumeObstruction.reusableModule: finite gauge-invariant basis plus positivity, Ritz upper bounds, tail floors, Schur complements and residuals is reusable once volume-uniform tail and coupling estimates are supplied

provedHere: self-adjoint positive one-plaquette Hamiltonian in the gauge-invariant character basis
certified enclosures for its two lowest infinite-basis eigenvalues
a positive certified one-plaquette gap at each tested coupling
notProved: a volume-uniform gap for a multi-plaquette lattice
a finite nonzero physical gap on a four-dimensional renormalized trajectory
continuum Hamiltonian existence and the required local field structure
the Jaffe-Witten theorem for every compact simple group

spin23Boundary.useful: the certified finite Hamiltonian module can test compact internal gauge sectors coupled to a separately constrained Spin(2,3) sector
spin23Boundary.notABridge: Spin(2,3) symmetry does not make the representation cutoff or volume estimates uniform and does not convert a cutoff-scale rotor gap into a four-dimensional Yang-Mills mass

decision: Hamiltonian truncation plus Schur-tail certification is a reusable finite proof module and proves the isolated SU(2) plaquette gap. Its tail floor and boundary coupling are not uniform under multi-plaquette growth, while its weak-coupling gap remains at the cutoff scale, so it does not establish the four-dimensional continuum mass gap.
